name: Fahrenheit’s reference-point thermometry

impact.note: Made thermometers comparable between makers; his scale and mercury instruments served science, medicine and households in many countries for generations and underpinned later heat science.

date.basis: Year of the historical document; work may have begun earlier.

events.statement: Fahrenheit’s 1724 papers described thermometry using a scale referenced to a cold mixture and human body heat.

links.statement: Fahrenheit recalled his visit to Rømer’s thermometers as the starting point for improving thermometers; NIST describes Rømer’s scale as an apparent inspiration for Fahrenheit’s.

evidence.supports: Fahrenheit’s 1729 letter recalls the 1708 visit as the beginning of his work on improving thermometers.
